minutes.headline: Design committee gave Taylor and Burns first-draft feedback: move school offices upstairs, side entrance, keep PAC cost separate.
minutes.summary: Taylor and Burns presented a first-draft program layout and exterior views for a new town hall building connected to the Ritter building. Members pushed back on school office placement, the exterior look, the entrance location and the connector. The chair also previewed PAC's space request and the Brooks House request, and the minutes were approved by roll call.

public_comment.topic: The APDC representative said he wanted to talk about the Brooks house, but not at that point in the meeting.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of November 14, November 20 and November 25, 2024
votes.outcome: passed — roll call, all members and the chair answered aye

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair estimated a build-out of the requested PAC space at a high per-square-foot cost, giving a total for white-box space only. PAC's minimum request is much smaller than its full request.
The chair asked the architects to separate out PAC's price from the roughly planned project cost.
A member asked about PAC's rent and the chair said PAC has saved money to outfit the space. A member suggested rent paid over ten years as another way to view cost.
Robert estimated the connector's floor area and members discussed its cost.

budget_items.topic: ARPA funding and Brooks House consultant
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said ARPA funding is about to expire, so a consultant for the Brooks House cannot be hired.

decisions.decision: Members present were broadly agreed that the architects may expand the Ritter ground-level town manager addition to the north if the space is needed.

Consensus that school offices belong mainly on the Ritter second floor; the basement is better for the ACE program, State Rep and veteran services; the town manager should sit closer to the new town hall.
By a slim majority the entrance should face Mass Ave, stay on the right side of the building, with a side entrance on School Street; some flexibility to enlarge the 1960s addition footprint.
PAC's portion will be priced separately, as a standalone building or annex, so it can be voted on separately.
The Brooks House request will be put on the next meeting agenda for detailed discussion; members were asked to consider Tony's concerns.
Architects will return with revised renderings in mid-January; the chair will review them with stakeholders and the select board first. The next meeting is January 6 at 5:30 p.m.

what_happened.line: Members gave the architects direction that school offices belong mainly on the Ritter second floor, with the town manager closer to the new town hall.
By a slim majority, members favored an entrance facing Mass Ave on the right side of the building, with a side entrance on School Street.
The chair said the performing arts center's space will be priced separately, as a standalone building or annex, so it can be voted on separately.
Members were broadly agreed the architects may extend the Ritter ground-level town manager addition to the north if space is needed.
The Brooks House request was deferred to the next agenda; architects will return with revised renderings in mid-January, and the next meeting is January 6.

why_it_matters: A separate price for the performing arts space means residents may be asked to vote on it apart from the town hall and Ritter project, so the two costs can be compared.
Where school offices, the town manager and the entrances go sets the size and cost of the building that voters will eventually be asked to fund.
